newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ will attend Hong Kong ceremony, rejects boycott.
newsitem.headline: NZ will attend Hong Kong ceremony, rejects boycott.

text.p: New Zealand will attend the swearing-in of Hong Kong's new Beijing-appointed legislature next month and saw no need to antagonise China further by repeating its concern over the body, Foreign Minister Don McKinnon said.
McKinnon told parliament on Thursday Wellington had no reason to join a U.S. and British boycott of the legislature's swearing-in.
It felt it had already made known its opposition to China's decision not to continue with the present elected legislative council after Britain hands back the colony on July 1.
"I see no point in carrying on a higher level of antagonism," McKinnon said in answer to a question.
He said New Zealand's four-person delegation at the handover commemorations would attend the swearing-in ceremony if they were formally invited to it.
A spokeswoman for McKinnon's office told Reuters on Friday that the invitation had been received during the day.

The delegation will be led by Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters, and include opposition Labour party foreign affairs and trade spokesman Mike Moore, former trade minister Philip Burdon and Hong Kong consul general Carl Worker.
Australia has also decided to attend all the ceremonies, saying on Thursday it needed to maintain a close economic relationship with China.
